## Read & reflect

**Read the article "Do native land crabs hinder forest regeneration on Socorro Island?" (Luna-Zuniga et al. 2025). Describe: \[2 pt\]**

1. The primary question(s) the authors are trying to answer.
The primary question was Whether native crabs Johngarthia oceanica are the main hindrance to 5 species regeneration or tree recruitment through seedlings predations on Socorro Island. The authors found that crabs crabs were a recruitment barrier for 2 for P. socorrense and S. Socorrense and the other prbomel was attributed to low germination rate. 

2. The experimental and sampling design. 

The studey was conducted  18 plots in total on Socorro Island, 6 for illex, 4 Guettarda and sideroxylon and 8 for psidium. They also employed controlled experiment to account for crab predation they have a control and crab exclusion area and tested the effects 


3. The statistical approach used. 

**Imagine you are reviewing this manuscript prior to its publication. Provide a constructive critique of the statistical analyses as they relate to the experimental and sampling design. What did they do well? What would be improved? \[3 pt\]**

To evaluate the predation, The authors used general linear mixed model where for a binomial1 and binomial.In the binomial where The response was the proportion of seedlings remaining after 10 days where treatment, species as the fixed effect predictions and treatment * Species  as the interactions and ID of the plot as the random effects. 
In the second model where they analyse forest regeneration,  the authors fitted nbinomia1  number of species perplot as the response variable and life stage, species, forest type, as the fixed effects predictors while species * life stage here the interactive effects while plot id was the random effects

However, the use of binomial and nbinomial1 was justified. The authors reported adjusted  residual plot but i dont see any plots, dispersion, spatialautocorrelation, zeroflation test. 

## Re-analysis

The data associated with this paper are available here: https://figshare.com/articles/dataset/Luna-Zuniga_etal_Regeneration_Socorro-Island_xlsx/29144249/1?file=54804050. Note that the file has several header lines; remove these in Excel prior to importing the data into R or use [readxl](https://readxl.tidyverse.org/articles/multiple-header-rows.html).

Based on your critique of the statistical approach taken by Luna-Zuniga et al. (2025), re-analyze the data to evaluate the effect of *Johngarthia oceanica* on the structure and composition of these island forests, specifically focusing on the seed predation experiment.
The authors mentioned the usage of DHARMa for diagnostic plot but i could tell exactly for what.


## Model development

**Based on the experimental and sampling design, which variables should be considered as fixed effects? Which could be considered as random effects? What distributions should be considered? \[1 pt\]**
The fixed variables should be treatment, species and the random would be plot_id and id_treatment 

## Analysis

**Develop a set of generalized linear mixed-effects models that reflect the structures described above. Include a model that includes the same response variables as Luna-Zuniga et al. (2025). \[1 pt\]**

```{r models}
#| message: false
#| error: false

# Paste your code in here!
crabs <- crabs |>mutate( prop_remaining = remaining / total_seeds) # recreating their model

m0 <- glmmTMB(prop_remaining ~ treatment * species +
    (1 | id_treatment),weights = total_seeds, family = binomial, data = dat_mod)

m1 <- glmmTMB(prop_remaining ~ treatment + species + (1 | id_treatment),
  family = binomial, weights = total_seeds, data = dat_mod) # removing the interaction term worsen the model so interaction is strong supported 

m2 <- glmmTMB(prop_remaining ~ treatment +
    (1 | id_treatment), family = binomial, weights = total_seeds, data = dat_mod)

m3 <- glmmTMB(prop_remaining ~ species + (1 | id_treatment),
  family = binomial, weights = total_seeds, data = dat_mod)

m4 <- glmmTMB( prop_remaining ~ treatment * species +
    (1 | site), family = binomial, weights = total_seeds, data = dat_mod)


summary(m4)

AIC(m0, m1,m2,m3,m4) 


```

**Evaluate the models using an approach covered as part of this class. \[0.5 pt\]**
I have fitted 4 Alternative models compared to the model used in the paper my the model in the paper which include treatment remains the best base on the AIC. Model with omitted interaction or replaced interactions with treatment produces poorer AICs

```{r modelselection}
#| message: false
#| error: false

# Paste your code in here!
AIC(m0, m1,m2,m3,m4) |>  arrange(AIC)
check_model(m0)

```

**Check your model diagnostics (i.e., are the model assumptions met) using an approach covered as part of this class. \[1 pt\]**

```{r diagnostics}
#| message: false
#| error: false

# Paste your code in here!

library(DHARMa)

res0 <- simulateResiduals(m0)
plot(res0)
testDispersion(res0)
testOutliers(res0)
testUniformity(res0)

```
